title: POC Weekly Sync - Quantization INT8 vs FP8
summary: Weekly check-in on INT8 / FP8 quantization experiments. Reviewed quality deltas on summarization and medical QA evals, perf numbers across A100/H100, and next steps for additional runs and artifact handoff.
topics: Quality impact on summarization and QA tasks
Latency and throughput deltas (p99, avg latency, tokens/sec)
next_steps: Redwood to share full benchmark spreadsheet + raw eval outputs by 2025-07-03
AtlasHealth to run internal counter-eval on their private prompts and share top 50 failure cases by 2025-07-08
Schedule deep-dive on FP8 op-fusion implications with infra team (proposed 2025-07-09)
Decision checkpoint meeting scheduled 2025-07-15 to confirm pilot go/no-go
action_items: Maya Chen: send quantization benchmark spreadsheet and raw logs by 2025-07-03
Leo Park: add KV-cache-on vs off rows to the perf sheet and run 2 more A100 replicates by 2025-07-04
Priya Raman: run AtlasHealth prompt set (5k prompts) on Redwood INT8 build and upload failures by 2025-07-08
Carlos Vega: validate network egress estimates for Dedicated VPC and share rough numbers by 2025-07-06
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining — can see Priya, Carlos, Nora. quick agenda: recap last week's runs, go over INT8 vs FP8 numbers, and decide next experiments
[00:08] Priya Raman: yep thanks Maya, excited to see the numbers — we had a couple of concerns about hallucination rate on clinical summarization so that's top of mind
[00:18] Leo Park: cool. quick note, the runs we pulled were on v2.3 quant pipeline, A100 40GB, batch sizes 1/4/8, and we included two FP8 permutations — one with per-channel scaling and one with per-tensor scaling
[00:34] Carlos Vega: are those runs with KV cache enabled? that was causing weird memory spikes for us last time
[00:40] Leo Park: good call — most baseline runs had KV cache on, but we added explicit rows with KV-cache-off; I'll point you to them in the sheet, those are lower mem but higher latency for long-contexts
[00:52] Nora Li: just to calibrate, what is our quality metric here? rouge? exact match? clinical correctness?
[00:58] Priya Raman: we mostly looked at ROUGE-L for summarization and an accuracy-style metric for the QA tests that map to yes/no or multi-choice clinical correctness. also track perplexity but it's noisy
[01:10] Maya Chen: ok let's go slide by slide. first up: SUMMARY slide — INT8 reduced token cost ~2.8x vs fp16 and FP8 reported ~3.6x savings in our piped evals. but nod to quality: INT8 showed 0.8% absolute drop in ROUGE-L on the summarization set whereas FP8 showed 1.9% drop
[01:30] Priya Raman: 1.9% drop on FP8, is that consistent across prompts or concentrated in longer summaries?
[01:36] Leo Park: looks concentrated on longer-context prompts >1k tokens — FP8's fused kernels impact attention stability at long seqs, some drift there. INT8 had more uniform small degradation
[01:50] Carlos Vega: latency numbers? we need p99 for real-time pathways and tokens/sec for batch scoring
[01:56] Leo Park: sure, on A100 with batch=1 INT8 avg latency was 180ms/token, p99 ~350ms; FP8 avg 150ms/token, p99 ~320ms. throughput (tokens/sec) INT8 ~2800, FP8 ~3400. on H100 FP8 improved further, FP8 avg 120ms/token
[02:18] Nora Li: sounds like FP8 is faster but higher quality regression — do we have qualitative examples of where FP8 fails?
[02:24] Maya Chen: yes, we pulled top 30 regressions, most are long-table summarizations and some structured outputs where numeric fidelity matters — e.g., dosages in notes got switched in 3 examples
[02:36] Priya Raman: that is concerning for compliance. can we do mixed-precision heuristics? critical fields at FP16?
[02:42] Leo Park: absolutely. we demo'd per-layer mixed configs: keep first attention and final lm head at FP16, quantize middle blocks. that recovers approx 60% of quality loss while keeping most perf gains
[02:54] Carlos Vega: what's the cost model here? if we go with FP8 + mixed fallback for critical routes, how does that change unit cost?
[03:00] Maya Chen: roughly, FP8-only run gives the biggest unit savings; mixed config increases cost by ~10-20% over FP8 but still lower than INT8? actually in our numbers mixed comes in between INT8 and FP8 raw savings because you sacrifice some quantization density
[03:16] Priya Raman: can you share the underlying raw logits diffs for the failure cases? we have a small labeling team that can triage
[03:22] Leo Park: yes we'll share raw outputs and diffs; they're in the shared spreadsheet under /artifacts/quant-v2/raw-diffs.csv — note: spelling/namespace may be off in auto-transcription
[03:36] Nora Li: I want to understand the private deployment implications — if we run Dedicated in our VPC, will FP8 kernels be supported there or do you require specific driver versions?
[03:44] Leo Park: FP8 support requires the runtime build with our fused kernels and a recent driver stack — on Dedicated we control the runtime so we can ship that; for Private on-prem we need kernel-level support and our eng team will provide a validated image — Carlos, that's an action for you to validate driver compat with the infra
[03:58] Carlos Vega: yes will check, may need to coordinate with our infra team around CUDA and container runtimes
[04:06] Priya Raman: were any hallucinations observed differently between INT8 and FP8 on the QA set? like assertive-but-wrong answers
[04:12] Leo Park: FP8 had slightly higher hallucination rate on open-ended medical QA (~2% higher on our labeled set) and INT8 had more minor phrasing regressions. For closed multiple-choice-style items the differences were small
[04:26] Maya Chen: scaling note — we ran replicate experiments x3 to smooth noise. we still see some run-to-run variance on A100; H100 gave more stable FP8 perf but requires updated runtime libs
[04:40] Priya Raman: any memory regressions? our goal is to serve 8k-token contexts and keep mem per request under 32GB
[04:46] Leo Park: with KV cache on, FP8 memory footprint is lower by ~20% vs FP16, INT8 similar. but the fused kernels for FP8 sometimes have transient mem spikes in our older runtime builds — fixed in the latest internal RC, which we'll share
[05:00] Nora Li: how about batching? does batch size improve FP8 advantage?
[05:06] Leo Park: yes, FP8 benefits more from batching; tokens/sec scales up nicely with batch=4/8. INT8 has smaller proportional gains from batching due to less kernel-level fusion
[05:18] Priya Raman: we also care about model compatibility — are these quantized builds compatible with our posh model variant that has extra classification heads?
[05:24] Leo Park: mostly yes, but heads that rely on FP32 ops might need explicit whitelisting; we've done a test on the classification head and it required leaving classifier weights in FP16
[05:36] Maya Chen: quick interjection — checklist for security/compliance: audit logs, KMS, SSO were asked last week. any blockers from quant side?
[05:44] Carlos Vega: quantization doesn't change audit/KMS requirements but we need assurance that model artifacts aren't exfiltrated during build. is there a signed artifact process?
[05:52] Maya Chen: yes we store signed build artifacts and can provide hash/signed manifests. we'll include that in the artifact bundle
[06:00] Priya Raman: back to quality — can we try the hybrid approach: FP8 for p95 traffic (non-critical) and INT8 or FP16 for p5/p0.1 critical routes? value in routing by SLO
[06:10] Leo Park: routing by SLO is exactly what Redwood's smart routing supports — can do policy-based routing to model variant per route and fallback on quality catches
[06:18] Nora Li: what's the overhead of routing? extra latency?
[06:22] Maya Chen: minimal — routing is decision logic in the control plane; fallbacks may add a few ms but nothing like model inference time
[06:30] Priya Raman: for the next experiment, can you run: (1) FP8 mixed with heads at FP16, (2) INT8 with per-channel scaling, (3) baseline FP16 — all on H100 and A100, batch=1/4, KV on/off and include long-context prompts (8k)?
[06:45] Leo Park: yes we can schedule that; will take 48-72 hours for H100 replicates. we'll add noise bars and per-prompt diffs in the sheet
[06:58] Carlos Vega: and please add network egress estimate per 1M tokens — that's part of my procurement modelling
[07:04] Maya Chen: noted, will add a rough egress estimate column
[07:10] Priya Raman: small ask — include example failure cases in the sheet with raw tokens and model output so our clinical reviewers can triage quickly
[07:18] Leo Park: will do, we'll redacted PHI and include synthetic proxies where necessary
[07:26] Nora Li: any blockers on your end to run the H100 experiments?
[07:30] Leo Park: just capacity scheduling — we have bookings next week but can carve out a window; should be fine
[07:36] Maya Chen: ok moving to the PERF slide — here's the table: A100 INT8 tokens/sec 2800 (sd 120), FP8 tokens/sec 3400 (sd 90); H100 FP8 tokens/sec 4600 (sd 60). latency p99 numbers as shared earlier
[07:54] Priya Raman: those sd look good, thanks for the replicates
[08:00] Carlos Vega: procurement ask: what are dependencies for Dedicated vs Private on FP8? I want a one-liner for our procurement doc
[08:06] Maya Chen: Dedicated: Redwood-managed runtime in your VPC, we supply FP8-validated images; Private on-prem: requires validated GPU driver >=X.Y and our signed image — we'll provide checklist
[08:18] Priya Raman: timeline question — if everything looks ok after the next replicate, how long to go from pilot to production?
[08:24] Maya Chen: typically 4-6 weeks for Dedicated: pilot -> infra proofs -> contract -> rollout. Private on-prem can take longer depending on approvals
[08:32] Nora Li: can we get an SLA doc and security whitepaper?
[08:36] Maya Chen: yes will send SOC2 + security whitepaper and SLA by 2025-07-03 along with the benchmarks
[08:42] Priya Raman: great. last bits: any thoughts on retraining or fine-tuning to recover FP8 regressions?
[08:48] Leo Park: quant-aware fine-tuning helps — a small 1-2 epoch QAT pass on labelled critical prompts recovered ~70% of the regressed cases in our internal tests. cost of that is extra compute but could be an option for critical routes
[09:02] Maya Chen: ok let's recap and close: action items reviewed, next steps set, and next check-in 2025-07-15 for decision checkpoint. thanks all
[09:12] Priya Raman: thanks everyone
[09:15] Nora Li: thanks
[09:18] Carlos Vega: thanks, will follow up on driver checks
